items.stem: What does a risk-based approach to customer due diligence require?

options.rationale: That is a rules-based, not risk-based, approach.

options.text: More intensive due diligence for higher-risk customers
options.rationale: Correct: a risk-based approach applies enhanced due diligence where risk is higher and simplified measures where risk is lower.

options.text: No due diligence for low-value accounts
options.rationale: Some baseline CDD is still required.

options.text: Due diligence only at account closure
options.rationale: CDD is performed at onboarding and on an ongoing basis.

items.explanation: Correct: a risk-based approach applies enhanced due diligence where risk is higher and simplified measures where risk is lower.

items.stem: Which TWO are typical red flags warranting closer review for possible money laundering? (Select TWO)

options.text: Transactions structured just below reporting thresholds
options.rationale: Correct: structuring to avoid reporting thresholds is a classic red flag.

options.text: Sudden high-volume activity inconsistent with the customer profile
options.rationale: Correct: activity inconsistent with the known profile is a red flag.

options.text: A salaried customer receiving a regular payroll deposit
options.rationale: Expected payroll activity is not a red flag.

options.text: A customer providing complete KYC documentation
options.rationale: Full documentation is expected, not a red flag.

options.text: A business paying routine supplier invoices
options.rationale: Routine expected payments are not a red flag.

items.explanation: Both keyed options are correct; all-or-nothing scoring requires exactly the keyed set.
